# AppointPanda: full guide text

Source: https://www.appointpanda.ae. Last reviewed 2026-10-21. General information only; not a diagnosis or a quote. In a UAE emergency call 998.

## Dental Implants
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/dental-implants/

A dental implant is a small titanium or zirconia post placed in the jawbone to replace a missing tooth root, topped with a crown that looks and works like a natural tooth.

An implant replaces the part of a tooth you cannot see: the root. Once the post has fused with the bone (osseointegration), it anchors a crown, a bridge or even a full set of teeth. Because it is fixed in bone, it does not rely on neighbouring teeth the way a traditional bridge does.

Implant treatment is a planned, multi-visit process rather than a single appointment. Most of the work happens before anything is placed: a 3D scan (CBCT) to measure bone height and width, a check of gum health, and a plan for where each post should sit.

In the UAE, implants are almost always paid for privately or through a dental add-on with a capped annual limit, so it pays to understand what is included in a quote before you commit.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 3,500 to AED 9,500 per implant, including the crown. Bone grafting, sinus lifts and premium implant brands are usually charged on top.
Treatment time: 3 to 9 months from first visit to final crown, depending on healing and grafting
Recovery: Most people return to desk work the next day. Expect swelling for 2 to 4 days and soft foods for about a week.

Steps:
1. Consultation and 3D scan: The dentist examines your mouth, reviews your medical history and takes a CBCT scan to check bone volume and nerve position.
2. Treatment plan and quote: You receive a written plan listing the implant system, any bone graft, the type of crown and the number of visits.
3. Placing the implant: Under local anaesthetic the post is placed in the bone. Most people describe the next few days as sore rather than painful.
4. Healing (osseointegration): The bone fuses to the implant over roughly 2 to 6 months. A temporary tooth can often be worn meanwhile.
5. Abutment and crown: A connector (abutment) is fitted and a custom crown is made from a digital or traditional impression.
6. Review and maintenance: Regular check-ups and hygienist visits keep the gum around the implant healthy for the long term.

Risks:
- Infection around the implant (peri-implantitis) if cleaning is neglected
- Implant failing to fuse, more common in smokers
- Nerve or sinus complications, which careful 3D planning aims to avoid

FAQ:
Q: Does getting a dental implant hurt?
A: The placement is done under local anaesthetic, so you should feel pressure rather than pain. Afterwards, most people manage the soreness with over-the-counter painkillers for a few days.
Q: How long do dental implants last?
A: The implant post can last decades with good cleaning and regular check-ups. The crown on top typically needs replacing after 10 to 15 years because it wears like any restoration.
Q: Does insurance in the UAE cover implants?
A: Basic mandatory plans generally do not. Some employer plans include a dental benefit that pays part of the cost up to an annual cap; ask the clinic to request pre-approval from your insurer before treatment.
Q: Can I get an implant the same day a tooth is removed?
A: Sometimes. Immediate implants are possible when the bone is healthy and there is no infection. Your dentist will confirm this after reviewing the 3D scan.

## Invisalign & Clear Aligners
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/invisalign/

Invisalign is a brand of clear, removable aligners that move teeth gradually using a series of custom trays, each worn for about 22 hours a day.

Clear aligners straighten teeth with a sequence of thin plastic trays. Each tray is slightly different from the last, so wearing them in order nudges teeth into a planned position. Invisalign is the best-known brand; several others work on the same principle.

The result depends heavily on two things: the quality of the digital plan made by the dentist or orthodontist, and how consistently you wear the trays. Taking them out for long stretches is the most common reason treatment runs late.

Aligners are removed to eat and brush, which makes them easier to keep clean than fixed braces, but it also means the discipline sits with you rather than with the appliance.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 9,000 to AED 25,000 for a full course. Short "lite" courses for minor corrections cost less; retainers are sometimes extra.
Treatment time: About 6 to 18 months for most adult cases
Recovery: No recovery time. Each new tray feels tight for a day or two.

Steps:
1. Assessment and scan: An intraoral 3D scan replaces messy impressions. The clinician checks gums, existing fillings and bite.
2. Digital treatment plan: You are shown a simulation of how your teeth should move and an estimate of how many trays you need.
3. Attachments and first trays: Small tooth-coloured bumps may be bonded to some teeth to help the trays grip. You leave with your first sets.
4. Regular reviews: Check-ins every 6 to 10 weeks confirm teeth are tracking to plan; refinement trays are added if needed.
5. Retention: Retainers are essential afterwards. Without them, teeth tend to drift back.

Risks:
- Slower or incomplete results if trays are not worn enough
- Tooth decay if trays are worn over sugary drinks
- Relapse if retainers are not worn after treatment

FAQ:
Q: Is Invisalign faster than braces?
A: For simple cases it can be similar or slightly faster. For complex cases braces are often more predictable. Your clinician should explain the expected timeline for your specific bite.
Q: Can I drink coffee with aligners in?
A: Plain water is fine. Anything else, including coffee and juices, is best taken with trays out, followed by rinsing or brushing, to avoid staining and decay.
Q: Do I need to see an orthodontist for clear aligners?
A: Not always. Many general dentists offer aligners for straightforward cases. For bite problems or significant crowding, a specialist orthodontist is a sensible choice.
Q: Does insurance pay for Invisalign in the UAE?
A: Orthodontic treatment for adults is rarely covered. A few premium plans include orthodontics for children or have a separate orthodontic limit; check your policy wording.

## Braces
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/braces/

Braces are fixed brackets and wires that apply steady pressure to move teeth and correct the bite, suitable for children, teens and adults.

Braces are the most versatile way to straighten teeth. Brackets are bonded to each tooth and connected by an archwire; the orthodontist adjusts the wire over time to guide teeth into place.

Metal braces are the most economical and robust. Ceramic brackets blend in with the teeth, and lingual braces sit on the inside surface so they are hidden from view, at a higher cost.

Because braces cannot be taken out, they suit people who want a predictable result without relying on daily willpower, including younger patients.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 6,000 to AED 20,000 for a full course. Ceramic and lingual braces sit at the upper end; retainers may be charged separately.
Treatment time: Usually 12 to 24 months
Recovery: Soreness for a few days after fitting and after each adjustment.

Steps:
1. Orthodontic assessment: X-rays, photos and a scan show how the teeth and jaws relate. The orthodontist explains options and timeline.
2. Fitting: Brackets are bonded in one visit of about an hour. Teeth often feel tender for the first week.
3. Adjustments: Visits every 4 to 8 weeks to change wires or elastics.
4. Removal and retainers: Brackets are removed and polished off. Fixed or removable retainers hold the result.

Risks:
- White spots or decay around brackets if brushing is poor
- Gum irritation and mouth ulcers early on
- Relapse without retainers

FAQ:
Q: What is the best age for braces?
A: An orthodontic check around age 7 can spot problems early, but most full treatment starts between about 10 and 14. Adults can have braces at any age if their gums are healthy.
Q: Are ceramic braces weaker than metal?
A: Ceramic brackets are slightly more brittle and can stain if you drink a lot of coffee or tea, but they work well for most cases.
Q: Can I eat normally with braces?
A: Most foods are fine. Avoid very hard, sticky or chewy foods such as nuts, toffee and ice, which can break brackets.

## Veneers
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/veneers/

Veneers are thin shells of porcelain or composite bonded to the front of teeth to change their colour, shape or size.

A veneer covers the visible surface of a tooth. Porcelain veneers are made in a lab and are highly stain-resistant; composite veneers are sculpted directly onto the tooth in the chair and cost less, but they wear and stain faster.

Most porcelain veneers need a thin layer of enamel removed so they sit flush. That step cannot be undone, which is why a careful consultation, a mock-up and an honest conversation about expectations matter more than the price.

Veneers change appearance; they do not straighten a bite or treat decay. Good candidates have healthy gums and teeth, or have had those problems treated first.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 800 to AED 4,000 per tooth. Composite veneers start lower; lab-made porcelain or E.max veneers sit at the higher end.
Treatment time: Two to three visits over about 1 to 3 weeks for porcelain; one visit for composite
Recovery: Some temperature sensitivity for a few days is common.

Steps:
1. Smile consultation: Photos, a scan and a discussion of shade and shape. Many clinics offer a digital smile design.
2. Mock-up: A temporary trial lets you see and feel the proposed shape before any enamel is removed.
3. Preparation: A thin layer of enamel is removed where needed and an impression or scan is taken. Temporaries are fitted.
4. Bonding: The finished veneers are checked for fit and colour, then bonded in place and the bite is adjusted.

Risks:
- Irreversible enamel removal
- Chipping or debonding, especially with grinding
- Colour mismatch if not planned carefully

FAQ:
Q: How long do porcelain veneers last?
A: With good care, porcelain veneers commonly last 10 to 15 years. Composite veneers usually need polishing or repair sooner, often within 5 to 7 years.
Q: Can veneers be removed later?
A: Porcelain veneers can be replaced but the tooth underneath will always need some covering because enamel was removed. Some composite veneers can be done with little or no preparation.
Q: Are veneers the same as a Hollywood smile?
A: A Hollywood smile usually means veneers or crowns on many upper and lower teeth to create a uniform bright smile. It is a larger, more expensive version of the same treatment.

## Hollywood Smile
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/hollywood-smile/

A "Hollywood smile" is a full smile makeover, usually veneers or crowns on most visible upper and lower teeth, planned to give an even, bright result.

The term is popular in the Gulf for a smile makeover that treats many front teeth at once, typically 16 to 20 veneers or crowns. Done well, it looks natural. Done in a rush, it can look bulky or unnaturally white.

Because it is a large, mostly irreversible change, the planning stage is the treatment. A good clinic will check gums and bite, may suggest whitening or orthodontics first, and will let you test the shape with a mock-up.

Ask to see before-and-after photos of the dentist's own cases, and look at the proposed shade in daylight as well as under clinic lights.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 15,000 to AED 60,000 for a full upper and lower makeover. Depends mainly on the number of teeth and the material used.
Treatment time: Typically 2 to 4 weeks once planning is complete
Recovery: Short-term sensitivity and a period of getting used to the new shape and bite.

Steps:
1. Full assessment: Gum health, bite, existing restorations and facial proportions are reviewed.
2. Digital design and mock-up: A digital plan and a trial smile let you approve shape and length.
3. Preparation and temporaries: Teeth are prepared and a temporary smile is worn while the lab works.
4. Fit and fine-tune: Final veneers or crowns are bonded and the bite is balanced. A night guard is often advised.

Risks:
- Over-preparation of healthy teeth
- Unnatural shade or bulky contours if poorly planned
- Gum inflammation if margins are not well finished

FAQ:
Q: Is a Hollywood smile permanent?
A: It is long-lasting but not permanent. Porcelain veneers and crowns generally need replacing after 10 to 15 years, and the underlying teeth will always need covering.
Q: Will it look fake?
A: Not if the shade, length and shape are matched to your face. Ask for a mock-up and choose a shade that looks natural in daylight.

## Teeth Whitening
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/teeth-whitening/

Professional teeth whitening uses a peroxide gel, applied in the clinic or with custom home trays, to lighten the natural colour of teeth by several shades.

Whitening works by letting peroxide break down stain molecules inside the enamel. In-clinic whitening uses a stronger gel with the gums protected; take-home whitening uses custom trays with a milder gel over one to two weeks.

Whitening only lightens natural tooth structure. Crowns, veneers and fillings stay the same colour, so if you have visible restorations near the front, plan for that before starting.

Sensitivity during and after whitening is common and usually temporary. Your dentist can adjust strength and timing, and recommend a desensitising toothpaste.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 700 to AED 3,000 per treatment. Take-home tray kits sit at the lower end; in-clinic systems at the higher end.
Treatment time: One clinic visit, or 1 to 2 weeks with home trays
Recovery: Avoid strongly coloured food and drinks for 48 hours.

Steps:
1. Check-up and shade record: The dentist checks for decay and gum issues and records your starting shade.
2. Cleaning: A scale and polish removes surface stain so the gel works evenly.
3. Whitening session or trays: Either a 60 to 90 minute in-clinic session or custom trays for home use.
4. Maintenance: Occasional top-ups with your trays keep the result.

Risks:
- Temporary sensitivity
- Gum irritation if gel touches soft tissue
- Uneven results where restorations do not whiten

FAQ:
Q: How long does whitening last?
A: Typically 6 months to 2 years, depending on diet and habits. Occasional top-ups with custom trays extend the result.
Q: Are whitening kits from shops safe?
A: Over-the-counter products are weaker and generic trays can let gel touch the gums. Professional whitening is supervised and more predictable.
Q: Does whitening damage enamel?
A: Used as directed, professional peroxide whitening does not damage enamel. Overuse can increase sensitivity, so follow your dentist's schedule.

## Root Canal Treatment
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/root-canal/

Root canal treatment removes infected or inflamed pulp from inside a tooth, cleans and seals the canals, and lets you keep the tooth instead of extracting it.

Inside each tooth is soft tissue called pulp. Deep decay, a crack or trauma can let bacteria reach it, causing pain, swelling or an abscess. A root canal removes that tissue, disinfects the canals and fills them.

Modern root canal treatment is usually no more uncomfortable than a large filling. The pain people associate with it is normally the infection beforehand, which the treatment relieves.

Back teeth that have had a root canal are more brittle, so a crown is often recommended afterwards to stop the tooth cracking.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 1,000 to AED 4,500 per tooth. Molars cost more than front teeth; the crown is usually a separate fee.
Treatment time: 1 to 2 visits of about 60 to 90 minutes each
Recovery: Tenderness for a few days. Avoid chewing hard food on the tooth until it is fully restored.

Steps:
1. Diagnosis: X-rays and tests confirm which tooth is affected.
2. Numbing and access: Local anaesthetic is given and a small opening made through the top of the tooth.
3. Cleaning and shaping: The canals are cleaned with fine instruments and disinfecting solutions.
4. Filling and sealing: Canals are filled with a rubber-like material and the access is sealed.
5. Crown if needed: A crown protects back teeth from fracture.

Risks:
- Persistent infection that may need retreatment
- Tooth fracture if left without a crown
- Rarely, a broken instrument or missed canal

FAQ:
Q: Is root canal treatment painful?
A: With local anaesthetic it should feel similar to having a filling. You may be tender for a few days afterwards.
Q: Is it better to pull the tooth?
A: Keeping your natural tooth is usually best if it can be restored. Extraction is quicker but replacing the tooth with an implant or bridge costs more over time.
Q: Does insurance cover root canals in the UAE?
A: Many employer plans with dental cover treat root canals as basic restorative care, usually with a co-payment and an annual limit. Mandatory basic plans often exclude it.

## Teeth Cleaning (Scale & Polish)
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/teeth-cleaning/

A professional scale and polish removes hardened plaque (tartar) and surface stains that brushing cannot shift, helping prevent gum disease and decay.

Even with good brushing, plaque hardens into tartar in places a toothbrush misses, especially behind the lower front teeth and along the gumline. A hygienist or dentist removes it with ultrasonic and hand instruments, then polishes the teeth.

Regular cleaning is one of the most cost-effective things you can do for your teeth. It lets the dentist spot problems early, when they are cheaper and simpler to treat.

If your gums bleed easily or you have pockets around the teeth, a deeper cleaning below the gumline may be recommended, often over more than one visit.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 200 to AED 700 per visit. Deep cleaning for gum disease is usually charged per quadrant and costs more.
Treatment time: 30 to 60 minutes
Recovery: None. Gums may feel tender for a day.

Steps:
1. Check of gums: The gums are checked for bleeding and pocket depth.
2. Scaling: Tartar is removed with an ultrasonic scaler and hand tools.
3. Polishing: Teeth are polished to remove stain and make them smoother.
4. Advice: You get tailored brushing and flossing tips and a recall date.

Risks:
- Brief sensitivity
- Minor gum bleeding, which settles quickly

FAQ:
Q: How often should I get my teeth cleaned?
A: Every 6 months suits most people. If you have gum disease or build tartar quickly, your dentist may suggest every 3 to 4 months.
Q: Does cleaning damage enamel?
A: No. Professional scaling removes tartar, not enamel. Teeth can feel different afterwards simply because the tartar has gone.
Q: Is teeth cleaning covered by insurance?
A: Plans that include dental often cover one or two cleanings a year as preventive care. Basic mandatory plans typically do not.

## Emergency Dentist
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/emergency-dentist/

An emergency dentist treats urgent problems such as severe toothache, swelling, a knocked-out tooth or a broken tooth, usually the same day.

Dental emergencies are usually pain, swelling, trauma or bleeding that will not stop. Many private clinics in the UAE keep same-day slots for urgent cases, and some open late or at weekends. Always phone first to confirm they can see you.

Go straight to a hospital emergency department, or call 998 for an ambulance, if swelling is spreading to your eye or neck, you have difficulty breathing or swallowing, or there was a serious injury to the face or head.

A first emergency visit aims to relieve pain and control infection. The full repair, such as a root canal or crown, is often booked separately.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 200 to AED 800 for the emergency consultation and X-ray. Any treatment done during the visit is charged on top.
Treatment time: 30 to 90 minutes
Recovery: Depends on the cause and treatment given.

Steps:
1. Call ahead: Describe the problem so the clinic can prioritise and tell you what to bring.
2. Assessment: Examination and an X-ray to find the cause.
3. Relief: Pain relief, draining an abscess, a temporary filling or splinting a tooth.
4. Follow-up plan: Booking the definitive treatment and, if needed, antibiotics.

Risks:
- Delaying care can let an infection spread

FAQ:
Q: What should I do if a tooth is knocked out?
A: Hold it by the crown, not the root. Rinse briefly if dirty, try to place it back in the socket, or keep it in milk, and see a dentist within the hour if possible.
Q: Can I go to a hospital for toothache?
A: Hospital emergency departments manage serious swelling, trauma and infection. For toothache alone, an emergency dental clinic is usually quicker and better equipped.
Q: Does insurance cover emergency dental treatment?
A: Many UAE health plans, including some basic plans, cover emergency dental care to relieve pain or treat infection. Cosmetic or follow-up work is usually not covered under that benefit.

## Children's Dentistry
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/pediatric-dentistry/

Pediatric dentistry is dental care for babies, children and teens, focused on prevention, gentle treatment and keeping young patients comfortable.

Children's teeth are smaller, have thinner enamel and decay faster than adult teeth. A pediatric dentist or family dentist focuses on prevention: check-ups, fluoride varnish, fissure sealants and diet advice.

The first visit is recommended when the first tooth appears or by the first birthday. Early visits are short and mostly about getting the child comfortable in the chair.

Baby teeth matter even though they fall out: they hold space for adult teeth and decay in them can cause pain and infection.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 200 to AED 600 per check-up. Fillings, sealants and sedation are priced separately.
Treatment time: 20 to 45 minutes for a check-up
Recovery: None for check-ups.

Steps:
1. Friendly introduction: A short visit where the child meets the team and has a look around.
2. Check-up: Teeth and gums are checked and parents get brushing and diet tips.
3. Prevention: Fluoride varnish and fissure sealants where needed.
4. Treatment if needed: Fillings or extractions with child-appropriate techniques, sometimes with sedation for extensive work.

Risks:
- Anxiety, which a child-focused team helps manage

FAQ:
Q: When should my child first see a dentist?
A: When the first tooth appears or by age one. Early visits make later ones easier.
Q: Are fissure sealants worth it?
A: For many children, yes. They protect the grooves of back teeth, where most childhood decay starts.
Q: Does insurance cover children's dental care?
A: Family plans with dental benefits often cover check-ups and basic treatment. Some government programmes for UAE nationals include children's dental care.

## Wisdom Tooth Removal
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/wisdom-tooth-removal/

Wisdom tooth removal is the extraction of one or more third molars, usually because they are impacted, infected or damaging neighbouring teeth.

Wisdom teeth are the last molars to come through, usually between 17 and 25. Many people have no room for them, so they come in at an angle or stay partly under the gum (impacted).

Not every wisdom tooth needs removing. Extraction is usually advised when there is repeated infection, decay, damage to the tooth in front, or a cyst.

A simple extraction is quick. An impacted tooth needs a minor surgical procedure, which an oral surgeon or experienced dentist performs, sometimes with sedation.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 400 to AED 3,500 per tooth. Surgical removal of impacted teeth and sedation sit at the upper end.
Treatment time: 20 to 60 minutes per tooth
Recovery: Swelling peaks at 2 to 3 days; most people take 1 to 3 days off work after surgical removal.

Steps:
1. X-ray or 3D scan: Shows the tooth's position and its relation to the nerve.
2. Anaesthesia: Local anaesthetic, with sedation available for anxious patients or complex cases.
3. Removal: Simple extraction, or a small incision and sectioning of the tooth if impacted.
4. Aftercare: Stitches if needed, written instructions and a review appointment.

Risks:
- Dry socket
- Infection
- Temporary numbness if the tooth is close to the nerve

FAQ:
Q: How painful is wisdom tooth removal?
A: The procedure itself is numbed. Afterwards, soreness and swelling are normal for a few days and are usually controlled with painkillers your dentist recommends.
Q: What is a dry socket?
A: A painful condition when the blood clot is lost from the socket. Avoid smoking, straws and vigorous rinsing for the first few days to reduce the risk.
Q: Should all four wisdom teeth be removed at once?
A: Sometimes it is convenient, particularly under sedation. Your dentist will advise based on which teeth are causing problems.

## Dental Crowns
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/services/dental-crowns/

A dental crown is a custom cap that covers a damaged or weakened tooth to restore its shape, strength and appearance.

Crowns protect teeth that are cracked, heavily filled or root-canal treated, and they cap dental implants. The tooth is shaped, scanned, and a crown is made to fit over it.

Zirconia is very strong and suits back teeth; lithium disilicate (E.max) and layered porcelain give the most natural look for front teeth. Metal-based crowns are now less common but still durable.

Some clinics mill crowns on site and can fit them the same day; others use an external lab, which usually means a temporary crown for a week or two.

Indicative UAE cost: AED 1,200 to AED 4,500 per crown. Zirconia and E.max cost more than metal-based crowns.
Treatment time: One visit with same-day milling, or two visits about 1 to 2 weeks apart
Recovery: Minor sensitivity for a few days.

Steps:
1. Preparation: The tooth is numbed and shaped to make room for the crown.
2. Scan or impression: A digital scan or mould is taken and a shade chosen.
3. Temporary crown: Protects the tooth while the final crown is made, unless it is milled same-day.
4. Fitting: The crown is checked for fit and bite, then cemented or bonded.

Risks:
- Sensitivity
- Chipping of porcelain
- Decay at the edge if hygiene is poor

FAQ:
Q: How long does a crown last?
A: Commonly 10 to 15 years or more, depending on material, bite forces and hygiene.
Q: Does getting a crown hurt?
A: The tooth is numbed while it is prepared. It may feel sensitive for a few days afterwards.

## Dentists in Dubai
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/dubai/

Dubai has the largest choice of private dental clinics in the UAE, from neighbourhood practices to specialist centres, licensed by the Dubai Health Authority or, inside Dubai Healthcare City, by its own regulator.

Most dental clinics in Dubai are private, so you can usually book directly without a referral. With so much choice, compare what each price includes, who will treat you and how easy the clinic is to reach at the times you are free.

Clinics cluster where people live and work: the Marina and JLT, Downtown and Business Bay, Jumeirah, Al Barsha, Deira and Bur Dubai, and the newer communities further inland. Many open into the evening and on weekends.

Licensing: Dubai Health Authority (DHA). The DHA licenses dentists and clinics across most of Dubai. Facilities inside the Dubai Healthcare City free zone are licensed by the Dubai Healthcare City Authority instead.

Insurance:
- Health insurance is mandatory for residents in Dubai, but the basic plans required by law generally exclude routine dental care beyond emergency pain relief.
- Many employer plans add a dental benefit with an annual limit and a co-payment, often covering check-ups, cleaning, fillings and root canals. Cosmetic treatment is rarely included.
- Ask the clinic whether it bills your insurer directly and whether pre-approval is needed for larger treatments.

FAQ:
Q: How do I check if a dentist in Dubai is licensed?
A: Use the professional search on the Dubai Health Authority website. If the clinic is in Dubai Healthcare City, check with the Dubai Healthcare City Authority instead.
Q: Can I see a dentist in Dubai without insurance?
A: Yes. Almost all private clinics accept self-paying patients. Ask for the price in writing before treatment.
Q: Are there dentists open late in Dubai?
A: Many clinics open until 9 or 10 pm and some open on weekends. Call ahead for emergencies to confirm they can see you.

## Dentists in Abu Dhabi
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/abu-dhabi/

Dental care in Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain and Al Dhafra, is regulated by the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi, with a mix of government hospital clinics and private practices.

Abu Dhabi has a strong network of private dental clinics on the island and in the mainland suburbs, plus dental departments in major hospitals. Al Ain, the emirate's second city, has its own established clinics, so residents there rarely need to travel to the capital.

Because insurance in Abu Dhabi is mandatory and widely used, most clinics work with the main insurers and handle approvals for you. Confirm your plan's dental limit before starting larger treatment.

Licensing: Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DoH). The DoH licenses healthcare professionals and facilities throughout the emirate of Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain and Al Dhafra.

Insurance:
- UAE nationals covered by Thiqa have access to dental benefits at participating clinics, subject to the programme's rules.
- Basic plans for lower-income workers generally cover only limited emergency dental care.
- Enhanced employer plans often include a dental benefit with an annual limit. Orthodontics and cosmetic work are usually excluded or capped separately.

FAQ:
Q: Who regulates dentists in Abu Dhabi?
A: The Department of Health - Abu Dhabi licenses dentists and clinics across the emirate, including Al Ain.
Q: Does Thiqa cover dental treatment?
A: Thiqa includes dental benefits at participating providers. What is covered and any limits are set by the programme, so check with the clinic and the programme before treatment.
Q: Is it cheaper to get dental treatment in Al Ain?
A: Prices vary by clinic rather than city, but Al Ain has competitive options. Compare written quotes for the same treatment plan.

## Dentists in Sharjah
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/sharjah/

Sharjah has a wide range of private dental clinics, many in Al Majaz, Al Nahda and Al Taawun, plus a university dental hospital, with prices that are often lower than in central Dubai.

Many Sharjah residents work in Dubai, so evening appointments are in high demand and a lot of clinics stay open late. Choosing a clinic near home rather than near the office usually avoids rush-hour traffic on the way back.

Sharjah is also home to a university dental hospital linked to a college of dental medicine, which adds a teaching option for some treatments alongside private practices.

Licensing: Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP). Dental professionals in Sharjah and the other Northern Emirates are licensed at federal level by the Ministry of Health and Prevention, and the Sharjah Health Authority oversees healthcare in the emirate.

Insurance:
- Health insurance has been made mandatory for private-sector employees in the Northern Emirates, including Sharjah, but basic packages generally do not include routine dental care.
- Employer plans with a dental add-on commonly cover check-ups, fillings and root canals up to an annual limit.
- Self-paying patients will find many clinics happy to give an itemised quote.

FAQ:
Q: Who licenses dentists in Sharjah?
A: Dentists in Sharjah are licensed federally by the Ministry of Health and Prevention, with the Sharjah Health Authority overseeing healthcare in the emirate.
Q: Is dental treatment cheaper in Sharjah than Dubai?
A: Often, yes, for the same treatment. Always compare what each quote includes, such as X-rays and follow-ups.
Q: Are there dental clinics open late in Sharjah?
A: Many clinics open into the evening because so many residents commute. Call ahead to confirm hours.

## Dentists in Ajman
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/ajman/

Ajman is compact, so most residents can reach a dental clinic within a short drive. It also has university dental teaching facilities alongside private clinics.

The smallest emirate by area has a busy healthcare scene for its size, helped by universities with dental colleges and their teaching clinics. Private clinics are concentrated in Al Nuaimiya, Al Rashidiya and Al Jurf.

Ajman borders Sharjah, so residents often compare options on both sides of the border, especially for specialist treatment.

Licensing: Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP). Dental professionals in Ajman are licensed federally by the Ministry of Health and Prevention.

- Mandatory basic health insurance for private-sector employees in the Northern Emirates generally does not include routine dental care.
